title: Noise as a Probe: Membership Inference Attacks on Diffusion Models Leveraging Initial Noise
abstract: arXiv:2601.21628v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Diffusion models have achieved remarkable progress in image generation, but their increasing deployment raises serious concerns about privacy and copyright. In particular, fine-tuned models are highly vulnerable, as they are often fine-tuned on small and private datasets. Membership inference attacks (MIAs) are used to assess privacy risks by determining whether a specific sample was part of a model's training data. Existing MIAs against diffusion models either assume obtaining the intermediate results or require training the shadow model on auxiliary datasets. translated_title: 噪声作为探针：利用初始噪声对扩散模型进行成员推断攻击
translated_abstract: arXiv:2601.21628v2 公告类型：替换交叉 摘要：扩散模型在图像生成方面取得了显著进展，但其日益广泛的部署引发了关于隐私和版权的严重担忧。特别是，微调模型极易受到攻击，因为它们通常在小规模私有数据集上进行微调。成员推断攻击（MIAs）用于通过判断特定样本是否属于模型训练数据来评估隐私风险。现有的针对扩散模型的MIA方法要么假设获取中间结果，要么需要在辅助数据集上训练影子模型。在本工作中，我们利用了一个关键但被忽视的漏洞：广泛使用的噪声调度未能完全消除图像中的语义信息，导致即使在最大噪声步骤下仍存在残余语义信号。我们通过实验证明，微调后的扩散模型捕捉到了初始噪声中残余语义与训练数据之间的隐藏相关性。
tldr: 本文发现扩散模型的噪声调度无法完全去除图像语义，并利用初始噪声中的残余语义信息提出了一种无需中间结果或影子模型的高效成员推断攻击方法。
en_tdlr: This paper discovers that diffusion models' noise schedules fail to fully eliminate image semantics, and proposes an efficient membership inference attack leveraging residual semantic information in initial noise without requiring intermediate results or shadow models.
